== Biography ==
William is the named father of Bessie in the 1682 Kirknewton index. He and [[Glasgow-3025|Marion Glasgow]] are the preferred identification of the 1681 intended couple, 69%; Marion is Bessie’s possible mother, 54%. [[McCook-217|Ann McCook]] remains an inherited wife and maternal alternative, without a supporting maternal clause in the inspected child entries.
'''William Glasgow''' has [[McCook-217|Ann McCook]] attached as his wife in the tree; the inspected child indexes do not establish that marriage. William was living in or associated with Kirknewton parish, Midlothian, Scotland, by 1682; Ann’s presence there remains an inherited claim.

Their daughter [[Glasgow-1545|Bessie Glasgow]] was recorded there on 21 April 1682, daughter of William Glasgow. Ann McCook is her attached mother in the tree, but the cited index does not name her.<ref name="Bessie1682">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch, Bessie Glasgow, 1682; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-ZQN FamilySearch record].</ref>

William was also recorded as the father of [[Glasgow-1318|William Glasgow]], baptised on 22 April 1705.<ref name="William1705">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch, William Glasgow, 1705; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-FY9 FamilySearch record].</ref>

William's own birth, parentage and death have not yet been established from contemporary evidence.

== Research Notes ==
=== Killycurragh generations, 20 October 2026 ===

The freshly read published transcription of PRONI T1959/3 distinguishes an older William of Killycurragh, the writer’s paternal great-grandfather, from his son William, the writer’s paternal grandfather and husband of Miss Cunningham. The younger William is the Cunningham husband, whose sons included James and Samuel. His son John married Margaret Glasgow after ordination at Coleraine and died at his father’s house in Orritor in July 1801. The surviving child, the anonymous writer, was born five months later; Margaret died in 1817. The separate church compilation identifies John Glasgow from Orritor, ordained at New Row, Coleraine, on 8 March 1796 and dead on 13 July 1801. The shared ministry, origin, name and death month strongly identify the husband. The writer separately describes Margaret’s father William as a son of James Glasgow and Margaret Rutherford; the two parental lines must not be collapsed into one grandfather.

Select [[Glasgow-1318|William Glasgow]] as the possible father of the letter-defined Cunningham husband at 36%. The letter supplies an older Killycurragh William, son of the Tullycoll/Tullyall William and brother of James (husband of Margaret Rutherford) and John (husband of Anne Mason). The 1705 Kirknewton child William has a named father William and a generation compatible with being grandfather of the minister ordained in 1796. The 1702 John baptism supplies a compatible second named son in that Scottish father cluster; the existing James-1025 family supplies the Irish James comparison. This is a positive but non-exclusive family-cluster hypothesis. The Scottish child’s adult identity and migration remain unproved. The 36% includes that identity uncertainty; it is not a confident Scottish–Irish bridge.

Select the letter-defined William of Killycurragh as Rev. John Glasgow’s father at 94% (strongly supported). The writer explicitly gives the writer’s father John, the writer’s paternal grandfather William and his Cunningham marriage. John’s Coleraine ordination, Orritor origin and July 1801 death match the separate New Row minister entry. This concerns the minister’s record-defined identity; it does not identify his grandfather with a Scottish baptism or upgrade his brothers’ later-profile matches.

Select [[Glasgow-2426|William Glasgow]] as Margaret Glasgow’s probable father at 84%. That profile represents William, son of [[Glasgow-1025|James Glasgow]] and Margaret Rutherford, which matches the letter’s maternal-grandfather family position. The letter explicitly names the eldest daughter Margaret as the minister’s wife and the writer’s mother. The profile’s circa-1735 birth and circa-1829 United States death are inherited claims, not exclusionary records and not corrected here. The letter calls William an eldest son; the circa-1735 estimate conflicts with the earlier estimated births of his attached brothers. Those unverified estimates require checking and are preserved here. This is the maternal grandfather, distinct from the Cunningham husband. Original records and an independent adult-life bridge remain to be found.

These are exact subjective assessments of complete relationship-and-identity propositions, not measured probabilities. The family letter is undated and unsigned and is read through Albert Rutherford’s published transcription of a photocopy, not an inspected PRONI original. The minister list is a derivative compilation whose independence from the family tradition is unproved. The Scottish adult identities remain possible: neither the letter nor the 1705 baptism supplies a migration, occupation, property or witness bridge between Kirknewton and Tyrone. The letter’s three-son family and second-cousin statement are internally consistent clues from one source, not independent corroborations. Existing people, vital fields and mothers are preserved. Miss Cunningham and Anne Rutherford are reported maternal names, not transferred to existing maternal profiles. The letter’s first-settler story is family tradition, not proof of the first Glasgow in Tyrone or of the surname’s origin.<ref name="KillycurraghGenerations20261020">PRONI T1959/3, [https://www.genealogy.com/forum/surnames/topics/rutherford/5445/ published transcription], read 20 October 2026; original uninspected. [https://cotyrone.com/churchrecord/ministers-pres.html Minister compilation], John Glasgow, New Row; derivative entry, not an original register.</ref>

=== Kirknewton household review, 20 October 2026 ===

The fresh public WikiTree capture marks Ann McCook’s motherhood confident(flag 20). The local review explicitly downgrades that inherited certainty to an unselected uncertain alternative: the child sources cited for it name only William. This is a reassessment of a tree flag, not proof that Ann could not be Bessie’s mother; no live flag or relationship is changed. William’s existing confident father role for Bessie is individually rated 98%, without counting it as new certainty.

Findmypast’s transcript names William Glasgow and Marion Glasgow in banns dated 10 June 1681 at Kirknewton and East Calder, OPR 689/20, item 1, p.39. It gives marriage year 1681, without a separate wedding date, ages, parents, occupations or residence within the parish. This transcript was inspected on 20 October 2026. Marion’s existing findings already contained the same couple/date from the supplied ScotlandsPeople index, OPR 690/10/82, FR51; these are derivatives of one event, not independent corroboration. The original remains uninspected and the archive-reference discrepancy unresolved.

Select William Glasgow-1026 and Marion Glasgow-3025 as the probable intended couple of the 1681 banns, at 69% subjective confidence for the combined profile identification. William’s record-defined Kirknewton father account is established by Bessie’s 21 April 1682 baptism, about ten months later. The same uncommon full paternal name, parish and close sequence favour identifying that father with the groom. Marion-3025 is the existing local child account indexed in 1655, whose name, parish and ordinary mid-twenties adult generation make her the leading bride comparison. Prefer this qualified reuse of two compatible existing accounts to leaving the recorded couple unconnected or creating another William and Marion. This selects the intended couple; it does not prove a completed wedding or a ceremony date.

Select Marion Glasgow-3025 as Bessie Glasgow-1545’s possible working mother, at 54% subjective confidence, replacing Ann McCook-217 locally while retaining Ann as an unselected alternative. The 1681 named couple followed by the same-parish William’s child in April 1682 supplies positive contemporary household evidence that Ann’s inherited attachment lacks. The mother is omitted in Bessie’s inspected indexes. The lower 54% includes the bride/profile identity, groom/father identity, completion or continuation of the union, and maternity; it is not direct record wording. This is a new preferred maternal hypothesis, not a documented maternity upgrade. Ann is not biologically disproved, and her other attached children and spouse hypothesis retain their prior status.

The alternative explanations remain: another William could be the groom or Bessie’s father; the bride could be another Marion, including the compatible Inveresk Marion-1429/Marione-3049 or Edinburgh Marion-3143 accounts. The earlier 1664 William banns item supplies another adult-couple comparison, not proof of one man’s remarriage. The older William-1087 remains a possible groom comparison if the bride is a different Marion; Marion-3025’s own William-1087 father identification is ungraded and cannot be used circularly to exclude that possibility. William-3974’s recorded 1671 childhood makes him a poor ordinary groom comparison for 1681, without validating the older man’s estimated 1660 birth. Marion’s 11 October/4 November 1655 date discrepancy is retained. Neither a shared surname nor a presumed cousin marriage proves the couple’s ancestry. The pair and maternity share identity premises and are correlated assessments, not independent proofs or mechanically multiplied probabilities. William’s John-3610 father remains 24%; no mother is transferred to his later children, no biological father is changed, and all vital fields remain unchanged.

Inspect the original 1681 banns and 1682 baptism for residence, witnesses, maternal wording and any marriage completion note; reconcile both providers’ register references. Test the 1664 groom separately and compare the other Marion households. Seek an independent William/Ann record for the retained alternative.

=== Kirknewton index wording checked 20 October 2026 ===

The Findmypast transcripts inspected on 20 October 2026 name William Glasgow as father of Bessie (21 April 1682), John (29 November 1702) and William (22 April 1705), all at Kirknewton and East Calder. None displays a mother, residence within the parish, occupation or witnesses. Bessie’s transcript gives OPR 689/20, item 1, page 39; the two later transcripts give the same archive reference and item but no page. This provider reference differs from the supplied ScotlandsPeople parish 690 references and must be reconciled against the original. No original register image was inspected.

The FamilySearch citations previously used to say William and Ann McCook were both recorded as parents were also inspected. VQ4K-ZQN is the father entry for Bessie, linked to child VQ4K-ZQF; it names William only. VQ4K-FY9 records the child William Glasgou and his father William, without a mother. Both display “Image Unavailable”. These indexes therefore do not establish Ann’s maternity or the couple’s marriage. The older claim that those citations name Ann is superseded; the earlier attached family and all citations remain available for comparison. An omitted mother is not evidence excluding Ann.

Retain Ann McCook’s existing spouse and maternal attachments as unproved tree claims; no person is detached or redated. The three same-name father entries do not alone establish one continuous 1682–1705 household. They supply no bridge to the older John Glasgow-3610’s Easter Newtoun household, so the selected John-to-William father hypothesis remains uncertain at 24%. The 1702 transcript supports 29 November as its baptism date, but does not resolve John-1544’s separate before-11-November field; no vital field is changed. This is a source-scope correction, not a new baptism discovery, father selection, confidence upgrade or component join.

Inspect the original OPR entries for residence, maternal wording and witnesses, and seek an independently sourced William/Ann marriage or family record. Preserve the distinction between a father explicitly named in a child record and identification of that father across later households.<ref name="KirknewtonIndexReview2026">[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4473863&tab=this Findmypast: Bessie Glasgow, baptism 21 April 1682, father William; OPR 689/20 item 1 p.39]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4473915&tab=this Findmypast: John Glasgow, baptism 29 November 1702, father William; OPR 689/20 item 1]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4473941&tab=this Findmypast: William Glasgow, baptism 22 April 1705, father William; OPR 689/20 item 1]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-ZQN FamilySearch VQ4K-ZQN: William in Bessie’s 1682 entry; child link VQ4K-ZQF; father only]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-FY9 FamilySearch VQ4K-FY9: William Glasgou, christened 22 April 1705; father William, no mother]. === Identity ===

This William was previously conflated with [[Glasgow-3974|William Glasgow]], who was baptised on 24 September 1671 as a son of Andro Glasgow.<ref name="William1671">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch, William Glasgow, baptised 24 September 1671, son of Andro Glasgow; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-F2B FamilySearch record].</ref>

The two men cannot reasonably be the same person. [[Glasgow-1545|Bessie Glasgow]] was recorded as the daughter of William Glasgow and Ann McCook in April 1682,<ref name="Bessie1682" /> when the William baptised in September 1671 was only ten years old.

The 1671 baptism and the parentage by Andro Glasgow therefore belong to [[Glasgow-3974|William Glasgow]], not this profile.

No contemporary evidence has yet been found establishing this William's date or place of birth or identifying his parents. The former structured father [[Glasgow-1554|Walter Glasgow]] was disconnected on 26 September 2026. Walter was christened in 1649, only about eleven years before this William's estimated birth, and no cited record names Walter as his father.<ref name="Walter1649">FamilySearch, “Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” Walter Glasgow, christened 23 September 1649 in the Kirknewton/East Calder index, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-FWL record VQ4K-FWL].</ref>

=== Marriage ===

Ann McCook is the attached wife in the tree; that relationship remains unproved by the inspected records.

No contemporary marriage entry for the couple has yet been identified. The inspected 1682 and 1705 child indexes name William only; they do not independently support Ann’s maternity or this marriage.<ref name="Bessie1682" /><ref name="William1705" />

Ann's current estimated birth date and her identification as Bessie's mother require independent checking; the 1682 index supplies no maternal age or name.

=== Drummore and "Walter" ===

Later online genealogies describe this man as '''William Walter Glasgow''' and associate him with Drummore. No contemporary source has yet been identified establishing either the middle name "Walter" or a Drummore birthplace or residence.

These claims should remain research leads rather than established facts.

=== Ireland ===

Later pedigrees connect this family with County Tyrone, Ireland. The presently identified records do not establish when or whether William himself migrated to Ireland.

The 1759 probate-index entry for [[Glasgow-1025|James Glasgow]] places James at Drumearn, County Tyrone, but does not by itself establish James as William's son or prove a Scottish-to-Irish migration by this William.

=== Priority Research ===

* '''Priority 1 — inspect Bessie's original 1682 parish entry.'''
** Obtain the original Kirknewton Old Parish Register entry behind the FamilySearch index.
** Record the exact wording, residence, father's occupation and witnesses.
** Confirm the spelling of Ann's surname in the original record.

* '''Priority 1 — locate the marriage of William and Ann.'''
** Search Kirknewton and neighbouring Midlothian parishes before April 1682.
** Search surname variants including Glasgow, Glasgo, Glascow and Glassgow.
** Search McCook and contemporary spelling variants.
** A marriage entry could establish William's residence, parish of origin or other identifying information.

* '''Priority 1 — inspect the original 1705 baptism of [[Glasgow-1318|William Glasgow]].'''
** Confirm both parents' names in the original register.
** Compare residence and witnesses with Bessie's 1682 entry.

* '''Priority 2 — reconstruct the complete William and Ann household.'''
** Inspect every Glasgow baptism in Kirknewton and neighbouring parishes between about 1680 and 1710.
** Resolve the parentage of [[Glasgow-1546|Andrew Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1544|John Glasgow]] from their original records rather than existing tree relationships.

* '''Priority 2 — investigate the County Tyrone connection.'''
** Work backwards from the earliest securely documented members of the Glasgow family in County Tyrone.
** Look specifically for records naming Scottish relatives, places of origin, executors, beneficiaries or other associates capable of linking the Irish family to William and Ann.
